title: Moka Onmae's 'Good Morning, Good Night, and See You Tomorrow.' Manga Ends in Next Chapter
content: Seven Seas Entertainment licensed the manga and will release the first volume in November. Seven Seas describes the story: When it comes to the topic of cancer, there is no one way to handle the news. For one young woman, Akiyama Momiji, the diagnosis leads her to reevaluate her life.
author: ANN

title: 5 Years Later, Major Crunchyroll Anime Suddenly Removed From Streaming With No Season 2 Hopes
content: Five years after it made its original debut, one major sci-fi anime has suddenly been removed from Crunchyroll (and slated to leave other streaming platforms) with no hopes of a second season.
author: ComicBook

title: The Killer Angel Within: Ameku Takao's Detective Karte Manga to End in 3rd Volume
content: The manga, based on Chinen's Ameku Takao's Detective Karte light novel series, launched in Good! Afternoon in September 2024. Kodansha published the manga's first and second volumes in January and August 2025, respectively.
author: ANN

title: Maki Fujita's Ka no Yo no Kemono ga Miru Yume wa Manga Ends
content: The manga's story centers on Sera, a high school girl who easily gets into trouble. She gets a detestable new bodyguard who crushes people without hesitation. Fujita launched the manga in Monthly Princess in May 2024.
author: ANN

title: Shonen Jump’s Biggest Sequel Ever Hits Its 10th Anniversary as the Series Gets More Intense Than Ever
content: Shonen Jump has consistently produced manga for decades, but only a few have stood out. One of the most outstanding manga of the 2000s is undeniably Naruto , a story fans often dub the perfect ninja series for how well it captures the genre’s nuances.
author: ComicBook

title: R-Type Dimensions III Game Launches Digitally on May 19
content: ININ Games announced on Thursday that the R-Type Dimensions III side-scrolling shooter game will launch digitally on May 19. title: Legendary Akira Creator Returns with New Anime After 12 Years
content: The creator of the Akira series, Katsuhiro Otomo, has left a legendary mark on the world of anime and manga, and his latest move may be his biggest contribution to the industry yet.
